publication.heroDescription: Essential science and technology news, simplified.

sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Last beluga whale leaves Marineland amid welfare concerns
cards.content: A beluga whale named Tofino was the last of 30 belugas and four dolphins to leave a Canadian sea park, Marineland, after it was shut down due to animal welfare concerns. The whales were relocated to various aquariums, but five belugas and one dolphin have died since the move. The relocation was done to prevent euthanasia, but experts say it's too early to judge the outcome, considering the whales were facing euthanasia and had been living in an ageing facility.

cards.title: German Police Detain Russian Man Over 2024 Cyber-Attack on London Hospitals
cards.content: A 28-year-old Russian man, Vladimir K, accused of being part of a cyber-crime gang called Qilin, has been detained by German police. The gang is suspected of hacking a blood testing company in 2024, disrupting services at several London hospitals and potentially contributing to a patient's death. German police are investigating the incident as part of their inquiry into Vladimir K and his associates.

cards.title: German Heiress on Trial for Abducting Children in Custody Battle
cards.content: A wealthy German heiress, Christina Block, is on trial for allegedly ordering the violent abduction of her children from Denmark during a custody battle. The case has sparked Germany's biggest espionage scandal in recent history. In a surprising twist, Germany's former intelligence chief, August Hanning, was arrested for treason and espionage, unrelated to Block's trial.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Bee Colony Viewed as Single Living Organism, Like Mammals
cards.content: A new study suggests that a honey bee colony is more than just a group of insects, but a single living organism that develops, reproduces, and ages like a mammal. The colony's development is compared to that of a mammal, with stages from embryo to adult, and it even undergoes biological aging and eventually dies after several years. This perspective could challenge common practices in modern beekeeping and raise questions about the colony's reproductive and developmental cycle.

cards.title: Astronomers Find Green White Dwarf Star Defying Temperature-Dependent Colors
cards.content: Astronomers have discovered a white dwarf star that would appear green to human eyes, breaking the temperature-dependent color limitations of most stars. The green star's unique color is caused by the interaction between helium in its atmosphere and other elements. This find can be used as a diagnostic tool to measure the chemistry of planetary material and shed light on the formation of planets.

cards.title: Webb Telescope Captures First View of Distant Brown Dwarf's Weather
cards.content: The James Webb Space Telescope has captured the first detailed view of the weather on a distant brown dwarf, WISE 0855, which is 7.5 light-years away. Astronomers used the telescope to track the object's weather patterns over 11 hours, observing changes in water clouds and atmospheric gases. The findings, published in The Astrophysical Journal, provide the most detailed time-series view yet of this cold neighbor and offer the first direct confirmation that water clouds on another world change thickness over time, similar to Earth's weather.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Roller Coaster Death Sparks Safety Questions
cards.content: The death of a man on a roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia raises questions about amusement park safety. Dr. Leana Wen, a CNN wellness expert, explains that serious injuries are rare, but not unheard of, and can occur due to the physical forces experienced during a ride. She notes that certain people, such as those with medical conditions or neck or back problems, may be more vulnerable to injury. Wen emphasizes that most people can enjoy amusement parks safely, but it's essential to be aware of the potential risks and take precautions, such as reading ride safety requirements and not riding if you don't meet the physical requirements or have a medical condition that makes the ride unsafe.

cards.title: tAN device shows promise for severe hypertension patients
cards.content: Researchers at Queen Mary University of London tested a small ear stimulation device to control high blood pressure that remains uncontrolled despite medication. The device, called transcutaneous autonomic neuromodulation (tAN), uses gentle electrical pulses through the ear to regulate blood pressure. The trial found the treatment was safe and practical to use at home, but it did not significantly lower blood pressure for the overall study population. However, a subgroup analysis showed that people with more severe hypertension experienced a greater blood pressure reduction with the active treatment compared to the sham device.

cards.title: Fat Before Carbs Regulates Blood Sugar in Mice Study
cards.content: In a breakthrough study, researchers found that eating fat before carbohydrates can help regulate blood sugar levels by slowing down stomach emptying and reducing the initial spike. This effect was observed in mice and may be applicable to humans, offering a potential dietary strategy to manage post-meal blood sugar rises, an important treatment target in diabetes.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: Southern India hit by heavy rain and thunderstorms, orange alerts issued
cards.content: Southern India faces heavy to very heavy rainfall, with orange alerts issued for Tamil Nadu and South Interior Karnataka. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) warned of heavy rain, thunderstorms, lightning, and strong winds in several regions, including Delhi and its adjoining areas. Heavy rainfall may trigger flash floods and waterlogging in vulnerable districts. Other regions may experience thunderstorms, lightning, and strong winds. The maximum temperature in Delhi is expected to hover around 31°C, while the minimum may settle near 18°C.

cards.title: Avalanche Sweeps Away Over 100 Sheep in Himachal Pradesh
cards.content: In October 2025, Joginder Chand, a 50-year-old shepherd from Himachal Pradesh's Chamba district, set out to migrate his 600 sheep and goats to warmer grazing grounds in Kangra district. Suddenly, an avalanche swept away over 100 animals.

cards.title: Srinagar's Water Crisis Worsens due to Climate Change
cards.content: In Srinagar, a water crisis has been ongoing for years, causing daily struggles for residents like Mehak and Zamrood. The absence of a regular water supply has led to the installation of tanks and a hand pump at their homes. Climate change is affecting Doodh Ganga, a vital source of drinking water, causing erratic water supply, low flow, and dry taps. The river's water availability is decreasing due to rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and declining snowmelt. The Kashmir Valley's 24 watersheds, including Doodh Ganga, are experiencing similar impacts.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Elizabeth Holmes caught on camera over 200 times
cards.content: Elizabeth Holmes, the former Theranos founder, has been caught on camera over 200 times by documentarians Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim. The footage is part of a new documentary,

cards.title: Celebrity Traitors Ends in Snooze, New Recruit Brings Energy
cards.content: In the latest episode of The Celebrity Traitors, the show's twist was that the final scene was a slow-motion build-up to determine which celebrity would fall asleep due to boredom. The traitors tried to make others yawn, but the outcome was far from thrilling. Meanwhile, new recruit King Kenny brought energy to the group, while Joe Lycett's desire to join the traitors raised suspicions. The next episode will reveal who is eliminated.

cards.title: Scottish Actor Hopes Fans Accept His Accent in Marvel Series
cards.content: Scottish actor Ruaridh Mollica, who plays Tommy Maximoff in the Marvel Cinematic Universe miniseries VisionQuest, hopes fans will accept his Scottish accent. He says speaking in his own accent helped him bring the character to life, and he's excited to be part of the show.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: UK's Strong Growth Data Amid Global Economic Uncertainty
cards.content: A global economic tug-of-war is underway, with crises from energy shock, trade conflict, and war holding back growth, while massive AI spending and resilience from smaller economies pull in the other direction. At IMF meetings in Bangkok, finance ministers highlighted the UK's strong growth data and its model pupil status, but uncertainty remains about the future direction of the economy.

cards.title: Tesla Unveils Electric Sports Car with Hover Capabilities
cards.content: Tesla unveiled a new electric sports car that can hover and turn in mid-air, but it's unclear when flying cars will become a reality. Other news includes Meta's trial over claims its platforms are addictive, a ban on under-16s using social media, and the release of Nintendo's Switch 2. SpaceX's Starship rocket exploded during a test, and the US president is considering selling his Tesla car. A digital detox expert shares tips to help you stop looking at your phone.

cards.title: Small businesses increasingly adopt artificial intelligence tools
cards.content: Small businesses are adopting AI tools for customer support, marketing, document processing and data analysis. Lower-cost AI services are making technologies that were previously available mainly to large companies more accessible to smaller firms.
